newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police reveal Nestle extortionist's voice.
newsitem.headline: German police reveal Nestle extortionist's voice.

text.p: German police on Tuesday set up a telephone line to let the public hear the voice of an extortionist who has threatened to contaminate products of food multinational Nestle.
Police also said the reward for information leading to the capture of the extortionist had been doubled to one million marks ($550,000).

In a recorded extract from a call to investigators, the extortionist gives out a telephone number in a distorted voice with an accent from the Westphalia region of western Germany. Police hope members of the public will recognise the voice.
The extortionist last week sent a letter to Nestle's German unit Thomy, claiming to have poisoned Nestle- or Thomy-branded products in 55 stores around the country.

The threat sparked a nationwide alert and more than 15,000 people flooded police with phone calls on an emergency number. Suspect products were cleared from the shelves but investigators found no trace of any poison.

Police believe the same extortionist has been behind several similar demands over the past year and stress that he is in the position to carry out his threats. Traces of cyanide were found in mustard and mayonnaise after one threat in April.
